title: SLO lifecycle: per-route quality contracts, staged cross-region rescue, and circuit-breaker escalation matrix
creator: Anita Kapoor
description: Define and ship a reproducible SLO lifecycle for per-endpoint and per-model routes that ties SLI definitions, error-budget accounting, and automated multi-region rescue actions with a deterministic circuit-breaker escalation matrix. Scope: (1) canonical SLI definitions for request-quality and latency for conversational and batch routes; (2) a single error-budget ledger per route with adjustable burn policies; (3) staged rescue actions: local throttles -> model-variant fallback -> regional failover -> emergency global throttling; (4) circuit-breaker thresholds and hysteresis parameters for each stage; (5) dashboards, alerting rules, and a concise runbook for on-call and SREs. This is an operational-first spec: emphasis on observability signals that can be used for automated choreography and human-in-the-loop decisions. We will avoid replacing existing global SLO governance but provide a deployable, auditable manifest that RBAC'd platform services can consume.
slis_definitions: Availability SLI: percentage of successful model responses (2xx) not classified as internal error within 99th percentile latency bound (see latency SLI) per 5m window
Latency SLI: P95 response time for low-latency routes and P99 for conversational routes; default bounds: low-latency P95 <= 120ms, conversational P99 <= 600ms
Quality SLI: evaluation-based pass rate against route-specific promptset (unit test prompts) measured on a 1h rolling window; default target 98% pass for critical routes
Fallback-compatibility SLI: ratio of requests successfully served by fallback variant without user-visible quality regression (>95% similarity on embedding distance and eval pass-rate criteria)
slo_targets_and_error_budget: Per-route composite SLO = weighted sum(Availability:70%, Quality:30%)
Example target: composite SLO 99.90% over 30d; implied error budget = 0.10% of requests
Error budget ledger: tokenized by route and tenant; burns attributed by absolute composite SLI misses and accelerated burns for correlated incidents
Borrowing rules: routes may borrow up to 10% of their monthly budget from sibling non-critical routes with explicit approval (automated or manual gate)
circuit_breaker_matrix: Stage 0 - Soft: transient p95 spikes for <15m: no circuit; increase logging and retain traffic; notify ops channel
Stage 1 - Throttle: sustained composite SLI breach for 15-60m -> apply ingress throttling to best-effort 80% of non-priority tokens (observability flagging) and reduce max-batch sizes
Stage 2 - Variant Failover: continued breach 60-180m -> route low-priority traffic to compatible lower-cost quantized variant or smaller context length variants; monitor quality SLI impact

Stage 3 - Regional Rescue: if composite SLI remains below emergency threshold after 180m or region capacity loss detected -> shift new requests to warm standby region per traffic policy with sticky session considerations
Stage 4 - Global Protect: catastrophic capacity loss (>50% capacity delta) -> enable global rate limiter and error-budget escrow that preserves priority customers and queued critical sessions
automation_rules: Automate Stage 1 throttle when p95 latency > threshold AND error-budget burn rate > 2x expected in rolling 30m
Automate Variant Failover only when fallback-compatibility SLI > 95% and smoke tests against representative promptset pass in canary pool
Regional Rescue requires both: (a) regional capacity alarm and (b) composite SLI breach > 3x baseline; orchestration will mark requests with metadata for tracing across regions
Global Protect automation must be gated by an on-call approval workflow (Slack + console A/B confirmation) to avoid cascading route shifts
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-route composite SLI, error-budget remaining (30d), burn-rate heatmap, top failure modes, regional capacity panels
Alerts: P0 page when composite SLI < emergency threshold AND error-budget burn rate > 5x for 15m
SLO policy audit log: every automated action must generate an audit event with causal metrics and active runbook link
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (this ticket): author SLO manifest schema and implement read-only enforcement hooks in router (no automatic failover)
Phase 2: implement automated throttle + variant failover paths behind feature flag and simulated canary
Phase 3: multi-region rescue orchestration, audit events, and on-call gating
We will reuse existing KV-cache tagging to preserve session continuity across variant fallbacks
testing_plan: Unit tests: SLO manifest parsing, error-budget arithmetic, burn attribution logic
Integration tests: synthetic load tests that simulate bursty token patterns and validate staged escalation triggers
Chaos tests: regional ejection simulation in lab environment to validate rescue choreography and metric continuity
Quality regression: run promptset smoke tests against fallback variants in canary before enabling automation
acceptance_criteria: SLO manifest schema v1 merged and documented
Router can ingest per-route manifest and populate dashboards with computed composite SLI and error-budget
Automated Stage 1 throttle fires under simulated conditions and generates audit events
Runbook published and on-call walkthrough completed with SRE sign-off
Two end-to-end chaos scenarios executed and green in staging
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal-only routes enabled for 1 week, manual monitoring
Beta: selected customer-facing low-risk routes for 2 weeks with automated Stage 1 enabled
GA: broader rollout with Stage 2 gating on compatibility metrics and staged regional rescue enabled subject to capacity smoke-tests

open_questions: What fidelity of quality SLI sampling is acceptable for low-volume routes (cost vs signal trade-off)?
Should tenant-priority be a first-class dimension in the manifest or resolved at runtime by policy service?
What retention window is required for SLO audit logs to satisfy compliance (default proposed: 90d)?
